description: Certificate canonicalization vectors for the root signature (security.md 11.1). 'cert' is the certificate object as authored; 'canonical' is the exact UTF-8 byte string that must be produced after removing 'sig' and applying the restricted-JCS profile (security.md 11.1). A conforming canonicalizer must emit 'canonical' byte-for-byte. One vector deliberately uses member names the certificate profile forbids, because it is the only way to distinguish UTF-16 code-unit order from code-point order; it tests the canonicalizer, not a certificate. Control-character escaping is additionally covered by an in-code vector in canon_test.go, since raw control characters cannot appear in JSON source.

vectors.name: utf16-code-unit-order-not-code-point-order
vectors.note: The one input where the two orderings disagree. U+1F600 encodes as the surrogate pair D83D DE00, so by UTF-16 code unit it sorts BEFORE U+E000, and by code point it sorts after. security.md 11.1 specifies code-unit order. Six implementations always did this; Python sorted by code point and agreed only because the certificate profile permits no such member name -- which is an argument that expires the moment the profile grows a field.
